new_statements.translation: Organisation of tonemes. Paradigmatically, the author [Mokrani] identifies two distinctive tones: /H/ and /L/. Syntagmatically, four tonal schemes are mainly identified: /L/ [kù] 'death'; /H/ [pyá] 'lie'; /HL/ [búyì] 'honey'; /LH/ [pìndá] 'peanut'. For S. Mokrani (2016: 601) 'Sigu seems to show a specific tonal constraint whereby, beyond two syllables, the tone is always low on the third syllable'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (382 pp., text; HAL tel-04957912). extracted text of p.50 (printed 'Page | 49') gives exactly: 'I.2.1.1.2.3 Organisation des tonèmes / Sur le plan paradigmatique, l'auteur relève l'existence de deux tons distinctifs : /H/ et /B/. / Sur le plan syntagmatique, quatre schèmes tonals sont identifiés principalement : - /B/ [kù] « mort » - /H/ [pyá] « mensonge » - /HB/ [búyì] « miel » - /BH/ [pìndá] « arachide » / Pour S. Mokrani (2016, p. 601) « Le sigu semble attester d'une contrainte tonale spécifique dans laquelle au-delà de deux syllabes, le ton est toujours bas sur la troisième syllabe ».' The reported quote is word-for-word; only difference is that the four bulleted examples were flat…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sigu is described as a two-tone (H/L) Bantu language with lexical tone schemes B, H, HB, BH on stems and a constraint that the third syllable of longer words is always Low; no statement about word stress or accent placement is made for Sigu. The only accent-related remark is B20-wide and diachronic (stem-final syllable regularly Low, read as a possible incipient 'processus accentuel').
new_statements.exceptions: None for Sigu; the diachronic B20-wide remark notes some residual H tones in stem-second position.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/stem-level tone schemes on (mostly disyllabic) nominal and verbal stems; citation forms. The Sigu-specific analysis is Mokrani's (2016), quoted and summarised by Koumbi Mabiti, who did no Sigu fieldwork.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources treat the same variety: Sigu/Sighu/Lisighu/Sisighu/siwu of Lastoursville (Ogooué-Lolo), Maho B202; Ibouily 2005 labels it 'lísí:wu, B 27' (Gabonese numbering) — same language, glottocode sigh1238. Koumbi Mabiti's Sigu section is a summary of Mokrani 2016, not independent fieldwork.

sources.note: Sigu section I.2.1.1 (pp. 43-49) is an explicit summary of Mokrani (2016): p.46 phonetic tone registers H, B, infra-bas, haut abaissé; p.49 two distinctive tones /H/ and /B/, schemes B, H, HB, BH, plus Mokrani's constraint that beyond two syllables the third syllable is always Low. No word-stress/accent statement for Sigu. Group level p.120: two tones in all B20 varieties; diachronic pp.237-238: stem-final syllable regularly Low, possibly 'une évolution vers un processus accentuel' (B20-wide). Author did no Sigu fieldwork; Sigu data from Ibouily 2005 and Mokrani 2016.
